threads.topic: DDCA D4910 no longer pooled with D1110 — confirmed with payer

messages.text: Weird one: DDCA portal shows a member with 2 cleanings YTD but the frequency panel says D4910 has 4 remaining. SOP math says 0 remaining (pooled 2/yr). Portal bug or rule change?
Seeing the same on two members this week. Both have SRP history.

Called DDCA provider services. NOT a bug: effective 2026-05-01 they unpooled D4910 from D1110. New rule: D4910 is 4 per rolling 12 months when there is documented SRP (D4341/D4342) in the past 24 months. D1110 stays 2 per calendar year. Written confirmation ref DD-2026-081.
SOP v2.3 still shows the old pooled example — do NOT use it for dates of service after May 1. I'll update the playbook this week; until then this thread is the source.
That explains three corrections this month. For pre-May DOS the pooled math still applies, right?
Correct — pooled for DOS before 2026-05-01, new rule after. Portal history view still displays pooled counts for old dates which is what makes it confusing.

threads.topic: Guardian IVR menu changed — new press-through path

messages.text: Guardian IVR changed. Old path (1-3-2) now dead-ends at claims status. Burned 20 minutes finding the new route.
New path that works: 2 then 1 then 3 then say 'eligibility'. ~8 min to a rep this morning.
Voice agent traversal success dropped to 61% on Guardian overnight — that confirms it. Re-mapping from a full-menu recording now; manual-dial mode for Guardian until the canary passes.
Call script doc updated with the new path and a note that the old one dead-ends.

threads.topic: FEP accumulators look wrong — plan year vs calendar year

messages.text: FEP member shows 1 of 3 cleanings used but the PMS ledger clearly has 2 this calendar year. Which do we trust?

Check the accumulator period label — if the member switched options at open season FEP displays PLAN-year counts. One of those visits probably sits in the prior plan year. Portal is right, your calendar-year assumption is what's off.
Yep, period label says plan year starting January. And TIL FEP does 3 cleanings not 2.
FEP is generous like that. Playbook has both quirks — the plan-year one keeps biting new folks, worth a bootcamp slide.

threads.topic: UHC CAPTCHA spike — INC-2026-055 running thread

messages.text: UHC flag rate 41% (baseline 12%). CAPTCHA triggering at ~30 req/hr/IP, previously ~90. Declaring INC-2026-055, P2 — voice fallback holding, throughput is the problem.
To be explicit for anyone new: we do not solve CAPTCHAs, ever. Shape capacity instead — widen the pool, cap per-IP with jitter, and batch per member like the MetLife pattern.
Batching rewrite cut requests per verification 2.3x. Capped at 25/hr/IP. Flag rate 19% and falling.
Back to 13% flag rate. Postmortem drafted. Real fix filed with provider relations: API/EDI accumulator access — the portal was never meant for this volume.

threads.topic: Claims beta: x-ray attachment rejections root-caused

messages.text: The two payers bouncing our x-ray attachments both silently re-encode uploads; our checksum validation then flags the response as tampered and we retry, which they read as duplicates. Fix: validate on their post-encode format. Patch in review.
That's 38% of beta rejections. If this lands this week the 90% first-pass bar is realistic for the Aug 24 week.
Canary on 20 claims tomorrow, full beta Thursday if clean.

threads.topic: Summit 6-month numbers are in — denials down 38%

messages.text: Summit QBR done. 6-month numbers: backlog 3.2 days -> same-morning, eligibility denials down 38% (9.8 -> 6.1%), 2 FTEs redeployed. VP RCM agreed to be a reference for DSO deals.
The line worth keeping from that call: 'my team trusts the green ones because the yellow ones exist.' That is the whole product thesis in one sentence — use it.
Adding it to the case study. Also flagging: their acquisition pipeline means a Scale-tier conversation at renewal — Lena, claims beta expansion interest too.

threads.topic: Reminder: no PHI in Slack (yes, pasted portal screenshots count)

messages.text: Monthly reminder because it keeps almost-happening: PHI does not go in Slack. Pasted portal output with member IDs counts. Case discussion belongs in the queue tool; reference cases by ID here.
Ops folks: redact before pasting, and if you slip, tell Maya same-day — deletion and log, no blame the first time. The near-miss process exists so this stays boring.
